name: Oracle version reconciliation (pin table for the conformance engine)
scope_note: Re-reads, on 2026-10-19, the official location of each artifact that the sweep (m02-m10, l02, critic x02) records with conflicting versions: IDTA 02099-1 and 02035-1..7, Catena-X CX-0143, CX-0160 and the generic DPP aspect model, GS1 Web Vocabulary, the UNTP Identity Resolver (redirect code, linkType=all), the Battery Pass Technical Guidance licence, and the canonical source ids of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 and Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1736. Output: pinned_values table, files_needing_correction list, and a short literature note. Left out: GS1 Conformant Resolver 1.2.1 text (prior record, not re-read), EPCIS, Battery Pass blockchain question (f02), the full-text access conflict for the taxonomy paper in l01/l02 (not re-checked), and every EN/ISO/IEC/DIN document (bibliographic mentions only). Digests: where bytes could be read through read-only gh api, a SHA-256 of the exact file and the git blob id are given; where only WebFetch was possible (ref.gs1.org, GitLab), no byte digest of the served file could be made and the digest column says so or uses the GitLab API's own content_sha256 and blob_id fields.
summary: This record is not a method description. It is the oracle pin sheet that a deterministic engine needs before it can compare a system under test against an open specification. Each artifact was read again at its official home on one date. For IDTA the authoritative bytes sit in the admin-shell-io/submodel-templates repository, where 02099-1 has folders 1/0/0, 1/0/1 and 1/0/2, while the content hub still shows 1.0 and the docs site shows 1.0.1. The 1.0.1 JSON and AASX are byte-identical to 1.0 (only the PDF changed), and 1.0.2 is the first folder with a corrected JSON and AASX, so a JSON-based oracle should pin 1.0.2 and record the hub and docs-site values as lagging. The seven 02035 parts also differ by location: parts 1 to 3 have a 1.1 bugfix folder, parts 4 to 7 have 1.0.2, and part 6 has no JSON in 1.0.2 (AASX only), so its JSON oracle stays at 1.0.1. For Catena-X, the published CX-Titan site shows CX-0143 v1.4.0, the GitHub main branch holds v1.5.0, the overview table still lists 1.2.0, and CX-0160 v1.1.0 exists only on main as a CX-Neptune item that its own banner says is not yet certifiable. The generic DPP aspect model has releases 5.0.0, 6.1.0 and 7.0.0 in the model repository, all marked release; CX-0143 changelog entries 1.3.0 to 1.5.0 name 6.1.0 as the version in force, the released EcoPass KIT 26.09 still names 5.0.0, and the unreleased next KIT names 6.1.0. GS1 Web Vocabulary 1.18.0 (published 2026-06-01) is current on ref.gs1.org, while the GitHub mirror stops at v1.16, so the engine must pin the ref.gs1.org file. For the UNTP Identity Resolver, the code 307 appears only inside the resolver workflow flowchart, in both the 0.7.0 source and the work-in-progress main source, and no numbered requirement fixes it; linkType=all is used in a 0.7.0 example but is a deprecated alias in work-in-progress main. The Battery Pass Technical Guidance PDF carries its own CC BY-NC 4.0 statement on the copy in the batterypass repository, so fixtures derived from it must stay link-only. The canonical ids for the two EU acts are the ones already in catalogue/sources.yaml.

maturity.spec_status: Mixed. IDTA templates: published (content hub), repository carries newer bugfix folders. Catena-X: CX-Titan current, CX-Neptune preview (go-live announced for 24 November 2026 on the CX-0160 page). GS1 Web Vocabulary 1.18.0 current. UNTP Identity Resolver: 0.7.0 released text and a work-in-progress main; both labelled suitable for pre-production pilots only.

maturity.regulatory_alignment: The IDTA, Catena-X and Battery Pass artifacts are industry or consortium specifications, not law. Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 is the legal base for the digital product passport (article-level content is in the earlier sweep file m01 and was not re-read here), and Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1736 concerns harmonised standards drafted in support of that Regulation. Nothing here shows that any pinned file satisfies a legal requirement.

pinned_values.note: Each row says what the engine should pin, why, and what was seen at other locations. sha256 values were computed on 2026-10-19 over the bytes returned by read-only gh api (raw media type). git_blob is the git object id of the same file. Rows marked 'not computed' could only be read through WebFetch, which returns converted text, not bytes. 'recommendation' is a proposal for the engine owner, not a decision.

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: No carrier artifact was in the conflict set. Carrier standards are protected (ISO/IEC 18004, 16022, 15459 and others) and were not opened.

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: UNTP Identity Resolver (IDR): resolver answers a GS1 Digital Link style path (for example /01/<GTIN>/21/<serial>) with a redirect to a default link, or to a link of the requested linkType, optionally filtered by language; the workflow flowchart in 0.7.0 and WIP main names HTTP 307 for every redirect arrow and 404 when no link type matches at any level; requirement IDR-07 (0.7.0) says resolvers must support specific, all, or default links. WIP main marks linkType=all deprecated (MAY accept as alias, SHOULD NOT send) in favour of linkType=linkset. GS1 Web Vocabulary 1.18.0 is the link-type vocabulary; the linktypes file (60 types, no version marker) is served at https://ref.gs1.org/voc/data/linktypes.

specs.component: Resolution section, query examples, resolver workflow flowchart

variants: any 3xx accepted by the GS1 resolver conformance suite (prior record, not re-read)
L03_data_exchange_protocols.observable_black_box: HTTP status and Location header of a resolver response on a loopback fixture; Link header or linkset JSON for linkType=linkset; behaviour for the legacy linkType=all.
L03_data_exchange_protocols.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 does not name a redirect code (not re-read in this task); the 307 choice is an UNTP diagram detail.

The 7.0.0 aspect release notes list many new operator, component and reuse attributes, which suggests tracking of the ESPR data points, but this is only an inference from attribute names.

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: Not in the conflict set. One persistence aspect does apply to the engine: oracles live on mutable URLs (ref.gs1.org unversioned files, GitHub main, GitLab main), so the engine needs a vendored copy with a digest and a retrieval date.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: Not in the conflict set. CX-0152 policy constraints are referenced by CX-0143 and CX-0160 but were not re-read.

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.mechanism: Not in the conflict set. Relevant to the engine only as supply-chain integrity of oracle files: git blob ids and SHA-256 digests in the pin table give a byte check.

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.mechanism: Version practice of the sources themselves: IDTA publishes bugfix folders (x/y/z) next to the hub entry and states in each README which issues were fixed (issues 187, 207, 208, 210 for 02099-1 1.0.2 and 02035-1 to 3 1.1; issue 263 for 02035-4 1.0.2); Catena-X changelog entries tie standard versions to named releases (Titan, Saturn, Neptune) and CX-0160 1.1.0 says bugfix versions of models become mandatory; the aspect model repository keeps older majors side by side with status 'release' in metadata.json; GS1 publishes dated archive releases.
variants: unreleased branch labelled with an older release name
L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.observable_black_box: A SUT can be asked which template version it serves (semantic ids and administration version fields), but the in-file administration version of 02099-1 is 1/0 across all three folders, so it cannot separate 1.0, 1.0.1 and 1.0.2.

L11_roles_and_governance.mechanism: Who owns the oracle and under what terms: IDTA (CC-BY-4.0 repository), Eclipse Tractus-X (CC-BY-4.0 model repository), Catena-X e.V. (all rights reserved on the standards text), GS1 (Apache-2.0 vocabulary files with the GS1 IP policy), UN/CEFACT UNTP (CC BY 4.0 per prior record), Battery Pass consortium (PDF CC BY-NC 4.0). These terms decide which files the engine may vendor.

end_to_end_flows.name: Pinning an oracle
steps: 1. Read the official location on one date (repository tree, hub, docs site, archive page).
2. Choose the file the engine would load (for example the 02099-1 1.0.2 JSON).
3. Compute SHA-256 over the raw bytes and record git blob id, size, licence and the other locations' values.
4. Store the file and the record together; mark mutable URLs as such.
5. On the next re-read, compare digest and version labels; report any drift instead of silently updating.
